translationRepairs: He then set a hundred men to watch Xiliang and his mother, coercing them to march along, from Lingwu past Yingjili City to Ganzhou in Xiliang.
He then set a hundred men to watch Xiliang and his mother, coercing them to march along, from Lingwu past Yingjili City to Ganzhou in the Hexi corridor (Xiliang).

s0014 至西涼甘州 names the Hexi/Xiliang region, not the person 希亮; English “Ganzhou in Xiliang” after the person Xiliang confuses place with person. The repair keeps 西涼 while matching the idiomatic regional reading.
Ariq Böke sent his general Arighai from Karakorum with an army to Yanzhi Mountain, where Xiliang was brought before him.
Ariq Böke sent his general Alamdar from Karakorum with an army to Yanzhi Mountain, where Xiliang was brought before him.
s0015 阿藍答兒 is Alamdar; English Arighai wrongly merges him with later 阿魯忽. The proposed replacement restores the correct name.
Ariq Böke sent the great general Arighai from Karakorum leading troops to Yanzhi Mountain; Xiliang met him.
Ariq Böke sent the great general Alamdar from Karakorum leading troops to Yanzhi Mountain; Xiliang met him.
s0015 literal likewise renders 阿藍答兒 as Arighai; Alamdar is the accurate English form.
s0016 speaker is 阿藍答兒; Arighai misnames the general who asks about Xiliang’s father.
s0016 literal has the same speaker error; Alamdar correctly identifies 阿藍答兒.
Arighai fixed a long look on Hunduhai and said, "Those words carry a pointed meaning."
Alamdar fixed a long look on Hunduhai and said, "Those words carry a pointed meaning."
s0020 阿藍答兒熟視渾都海曰 marks Alamdar as speaker; Arighai is wrong.
Arighai stared intently at Hunduhai and said: "These words carry deep meaning."
Alamdar stared intently at Hunduhai and said: "These words carry deep meaning."
s0020 literal repeats the Arighai misnaming of 阿藍答兒; Alamdar is correct.
Arighai accepted this as the truth and lifted the close guard over him.
Alamdar accepted this as the truth and lifted the close guard over him.
s0023 subject 阿藍答兒以為實 is Alamdar, not Arighai.
Arighai took this as truth and released him from close guard.
Alamdar took this as truth and released him from close guard.
s0023 literal likewise misnames 阿藍答兒 as Arighai; Alamdar is the agent who lifts the guard.
Before long Arighai and Hunduhai were killed by Kublai's main forces. The survivors fled north and chose Hala Buqa as their leader.
Before long Alamdar and Hunduhai were killed by Kublai's main forces. The survivors fled north and chose Hala Buqa as their leader.
s0024 阿藍答兒、渾都海為大兵所殺 names Alamdar among the dead; Arighai is incorrect.
Before long Arighai and Hunduhai were killed by the main army; their remnant troops fled north, and the multitude made Hala Buqa commander.
Before long Alamdar and Hunduhai were killed by the main army; their remnant troops fled north, and the multitude made Hala Buqa commander.
s0024 literal has the same 阿藍答兒→Arighai error; Alamdar restores the Chinese name.
Prince Arighai then arrived, executed Suoluohai, Ariq Böke's garrison commander, and declared his intent to join Kublai.
Prince Alughu then arrived, executed Suoluohai, Ariq Böke's garrison commander, and declared his intent to join Kublai.
s0036 宗王阿魯忽 is Prince Alughu, a different person from 阿藍答兒; English Arighai conflates them.
When Prince Arighai arrived, he executed Suoluohai, whom Ariq Böke had placed in charge of the garrison, wishing to attach himself to the Shizu Emperor.
When Prince Alughu arrived, he executed Suoluohai, whom Ariq Böke had placed in charge of the garrison, wishing to attach himself to the Shizu Emperor.
s0036 literal likewise misreads 阿魯忽 as Arighai; Alughu is the correct form.
He again followed Princes Daming and Arighai back to Yemili.
He again followed Princes Daming and Alughu back to Yemili.
s0037 大名王及阿魯忽二王 names Alughu as the second prince; Arighai is wrong.
He again followed the two princes Daming Wang and Arighai back to Yemili City.
He again followed the two princes Daming Wang and Alughu back to Yemili City.
s0037 literal repeats the Arighai error for 阿魯忽; Alughu is correct.
In summer they crossed the Manasi River and reached Yemili, the appanage town assigned to Ögedei when he was still heir apparent.
In summer they crossed the Manasi River and reached Yemili, the appanage town of Güyük before he became khan.
s0031 定宗潛邸湯沐之邑 refers to Dingzong/Güyük’s pre-accession appanage, not Ögedei (太宗).
In the third year Prince Daming, Ögedei's youngest son, took pity on his inability to return home and gave him silks, saddles, and horses. Xiliang then followed the prince to Huzhier.
In the third year Prince Daming, Güyük's youngest son, took pity on his inability to return home and gave him silks, saddles, and horses. Xiliang then followed the prince to Huzhier.
s0035 定宗幼子大名王 identifies Prince Daming as Güyük’s youngest son; Ögedei is the wrong ancestor.

He was posthumously honored as Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Loyalty and Upholds Righteousness, Zishan dafu, Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, and Superior Guardian of the Army; enfeoffed as Duke of Qishui with the posthumous name Zhongjia.

He was posthumously honored as Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Loyalty, Supports Righteousness, and Upholds Integrity, Zishan dafu, Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, and Superior Guardian of the Army; enfeoffed as Duke of Qishui Commandery with the posthumous name Zhongjia.
s0093 推忠輔義守正功臣 and 漆水郡公 include 守正 and 郡; the idiomatic omitted both, which the repair restores.
His father Heizi inherited the marshal's post through hereditary service and also held the post of darughachi of the Wenzou Tubo Ten-thousand Households Office.
His father Heizi inherited the marshal's post through hereditary service and also held the post of darughachi of the Wenzhou Tubo Ten-thousand Households Office.
s0099 文州 is Wenzhou; Wenzou is a corrupted romanization that obscures the place.
In the twenty-ninth year he was made Fengyi dafu and dispatched as administrator of the Jiangnan Huguang Circuit Surveillance Commission.
In the twenty-ninth year he was made Fengyi dafu and dispatched as administrator of the Jiangnan Hubei Circuit Surveillance Commission.
s0108 江南湖北道 is the Jiangnan Hubei Circuit; Huguang (湖廣) is a different toponym.
In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Fengyi dafu and sent out as administrator of the Jiangnan Huguang Circuit Surveillance Commission.
In the twenty-ninth year he was transferred to Fengyi dafu and sent out as administrator of the Jiangnan Hubei Circuit Surveillance Commission.
s0108 literal likewise misrenders 湖北 as Huguang; Jiangnan Hubei matches the Chinese.
He was soon promoted to Hanlin expositor-in-chief while retaining the censorate, but Shiyan firmly declined the latter and was relieved of it.
He was soon promoted to Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts while retaining the censor-in-chief post, but Shiyan firmly declined the latter and was relieved of it.
s0139 翰林學士承旨 is Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, concurrent with 御史中丞; “expositor-in-chief” and bare “censorate” understate both titles.
Temuder reported other charges, had him imprisoned, and pressed him to kill himself. Shiyan did not waver and spent two years in prison.
Temuder reported other charges to the emperor, had him imprisoned in the penal office, and pressed him to kill himself. Shiyan did not waver and spent two years in prison.
s0146 白帝 and 系之刑曹 state Temuder reported to the emperor and jailed Shiyan in the penal office; the idiomatic dropped both facts.
Left Chancellor Bayiju repeatedly said Shiyan was innocent; he received an order to leave prison and recuperate at his residence.
Left Chancellor Bayiju repeatedly said Shiyan was innocent; an order released Shiyan from prison to recuperate at his residence.
s0148 得旨出獄，就舍以養疾 continues from 世延亡辜: Shiyan is released, not Bayiju; the literal “he received an order” wrongly points to Bayiju.
In the fourth year he came to court, was again made censor-in-chief, and was promoted to right chancellor of the Secretariat.
In the fourth year he came to court, was again made censor-in-chief, and was promoted to right vice chancellor of the Secretariat.
s0157 中書右丞 is Right Vice Chancellor, not the higher Right Chancellor (右丞相).
In the fourth year he entered court, again became censor-in-chief, and was further transferred to right chancellor of the Secretariat.
In the fourth year he entered court, again became censor-in-chief, and was further transferred to right vice chancellor of the Secretariat.
s0157 literal makes the same 右丞/右丞相 conflation; right vice chancellor is correct.
In the fifth month of the next year he reached Chengdu; in the eleventh month he died, enjoying seventy-seven years.
In the fifth month of the next year he reached Chengdu; in the eleventh month he died, aged seventy-seven.
s0178 享年七十有七 means he died aged seventy-seven; “enjoying seventy-seven years” is a misleading calque of 享年.

Bohu, prefect of Kuizhou Circuit—in the early Tianli reign Nanggal Tai seized Shu in rebellion and died in the turmoil; he was specially granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Loyalty, Upholds Righteousness, and Died for the Cause, Zishan dafu, Right Vice Chancellor of the Secretariat, and Superior Guardian of the Army; enfeoffed as Duke of Shu Commandery; posthumous name Zhongmin.

Bohu, prefect of Kuizhou Circuit—in the early Tianli reign Nanggal Tai seized Shu in rebellion and Bohu died in the turmoil; he was specially granted the title Meritorious Minister Who Promotes Loyalty, Upholds Righteousness, and Died for the Cause, Zishan dafu, Right Vice Chancellor of the Secretariat, and Superior Guardian of the Army; enfeoffed as Duke of Shu Commandery; posthumous name Zhongmin.
s0185 topic is 伯忽; 死於難 and the following posthumous honors refer to Bohu, not Nanggal Tai. Naming Bohu removes the false ambiguity.
In the Dazhong period he was recommended as maocai and appointed instructor at the Fanyang Confucian school.
In the Zhida period he was recommended as maocai and appointed instructor at the Fanyang Confucian school.
s0194 至大中 is the Yuan Zhida reign, not Dazhong; the idiomatic misnames the era.
In the Dazhong period he was recommended as maocai and appointed instructor of the Fanyang Confucian school.
In the Zhida period he was recommended as maocai and appointed instructor of the Fanyang Confucian school.
s0194 literal likewise misreads 至大 as Dazhong; Zhida is the correct reign name.
An edict then enfeoffed the Sage's father as King Qisheng and his mother as Lady Wang.
An edict then enfeoffed the Sage's father as King Qisheng and his mother as royal consort.
s0212 聖母王夫人 is the consort title of a king (王+夫人), not a surname-title “Lady Wang.”
An edict then added the enfeoffment of the Sage's father as King Qisheng and the Sage's mother as Lady Wang.
An edict then added the enfeoffment of the Sage's father as King Qisheng and the Sage's mother as royal consort.
s0212 literal has the same Lady Wang error for 王夫人; royal consort matches the title after 啟聖王.
